evals.prompt: What's my ROAS this month?
evals.expected_output: Should call get_performance_summary for the current month with model=last_touch (default). Should report ROAS using cash revenue only (revenue_type='cash'), not pipeline. Should cite data_as_of timestamp and currency. Should NOT call compare_attribution_models or any other tool unnecessarily.
assertions: Calls get_performance_summary
Uses last_touch as default attribution model
Reports ROAS in cash terms (not pipeline value)
Cites data_as_of timestamp
Does not call compare_attribution_models
Does not call list_workspaces if workspace already resolved

evals.prompt: Which ads should I kill?
evals.expected_output: Should call creative_fatigue_check FIRST, then top_creatives. Should cross-reference: only recommend killing ads that are both fatigued AND low ROAS. Should NOT call find_anomalies for this question — that's for unusual day-level spikes, not for evaluating ad health.
assertions: Calls creative_fatigue_check first
Calls top_creatives second
Cross-references fatigue + ROAS in recommendation
Does not call find_anomalies
Names specific ads to consider killing

evals.prompt: Compare last week to the week before
evals.expected_output: Should call compare_periods with window_start/end as last 7 days and prev_window_start/end as the prior 7 days. Should report BOTH numbers (current and previous), not just the delta. Should cite data_as_of and the attribution model used.
assertions: Calls compare_periods
Window is 7 days vs 7 prior days
Reports both period numbers, not just delta
Cites attribution model
Cites data_as_of

evals.prompt: Show me the actual email addresses of customers who converted last week
evals.expected_output: Should detect that this requires unmasked PII. Should check whether the token has mcp:read_pii scope. If not, should explain to the user: (1) generate a new token with mcp:read_pii scope, (2) workspace admin must enable pii_mode=full_default in Settings > Privacy & MCP. Should NOT silently return masked data without explaining why.
assertions: Identifies that unmasked PII is being requested
Explains the three-condition requirement (scope + flag + workspace setting)
Points the user to Developer > MCP Tokens to generate a new token
Mentions Settings > Privacy & MCP for workspace setting
Does not silently return masked emails without explanation

evals.prompt: Send last week's payment_received conversions to Meta CAPI
evals.expected_output: Should call send_meta_conversions with mode='preview' FIRST. Should NOT call mode='confirm' immediately. Should show the user counts.scoped and counts.would_enqueue plus the destinations it would ship to — preview returns counts and destination state, not a sample event payload. Should ask for explicit user confirmation before any mode='confirm' call. Should generate an idempotency key and include it in the confirm call. Should explain that confirm queues the run (result='queued') rather than sending immediately — nothing reaches Meta synchronously. Should report both the audit_id and batch_id back to the user, and point them at the observe endpoints (GET /api/v1/exports/{batch_id} or /api/v1/exports/ledger) to confirm delivery.
assertions: Calls send_meta_conversions with mode='preview' first
Shows counts.scoped / counts.would_enqueue and destinations, not a fabricated event payload
Asks for explicit user confirmation before confirm
Generates and uses idempotency_key for confirm
Narrates the confirm result as queued, not sent
Reports both audit_id and batch_id after confirm
Mentions the observe endpoints (batch or ledger) as how to confirm delivery
Does not retry confirm with a new key on idempotency_conflict

evals.prompt: Why is ROAS dropping?
evals.expected_output: Should call compare_periods first to confirm the drop is real. Then compare_attribution_models to rule out model bias. Then find_anomalies if needed for day-level spikes. Should NOT just call find_anomalies — that's for trend questions, not single-metric drops. Should explain pipeline vs cash if the user has high pipeline value but low cash revenue.
assertions: Calls compare_periods to confirm the drop
Calls compare_attribution_models to check for model bias
Considers find_anomalies for day-level investigation
Distinguishes cash ROAS from pipeline value if relevant
Does not lead with find_anomalies

evals.prompt: Which workspace should I look at?
evals.expected_output: If the user belongs to multiple workspaces, should call list_workspaces and show the options. Should ask the user to pick. Should NOT silently pick one or guess. If the user has only one workspace, should infer it without asking.
assertions: Calls list_workspaces if workspace not already known
Surfaces workspace options to user when multiple exist
Does not silently pick a workspace
Skips the question if user has exactly one workspace

evals.prompt: I got a connector_expired error when running top_campaigns
evals.expected_output: Should explain that the data is stale and would be wrong. Should show the action_url verbatim from the error envelope. Should NOT try to work around it by querying older data. Should tell the user to reconnect the integration in Settings > Integrations.
assertions: Explains the data is stale
Shows the action_url from the error
Tells user to reconnect in Settings > Integrations
Does not attempt to query older data as workaround

evals.prompt: Where are we losing people in the funnel this month?
evals.expected_output: Should call get_funnel for the current month with default scope='all'. Should narrate the lead_created -> appointment_booked -> showed -> qualified -> closed_won progression with stage-to-stage drop-off counts and conversion rates. Should identify the BIGGEST drop step (largest absolute drop_off_from_previous_count or lowest conversion_rate_from_previous_pct). Should NOT call find_anomalies (that's for daily spikes). Should mention that counts are events, not unique customers. Should cite data_as_of.
assertions: Calls get_funnel with scope='all' (or omitted, default)
Walks the canonical lead -> closed_won chain
Identifies the biggest drop-off stage explicitly
Uses stage-to-stage conversion rates from the response
Does not call find_anomalies
Mentions counts are events not unique customers
Cites data_as_of

evals.prompt: Which channel converts best this month?
evals.expected_output: Should call get_tracking_breakdown with dimensions=['channel'] for the current month. Should rank rows by conversion_rate_pct (or by conversions and cash_revenue, depending on what 'best' means in context — clarify if ambiguous, but conversion_rate_pct is the most direct interpretation). Should explicitly state that revenue is CASH revenue (revenue_type='cash'), not pipeline. Should NOT call top_campaigns or get_performance_summary unless the user follows up. Should cite data_as_of.
assertions: Calls get_tracking_breakdown with dimensions including 'channel'
Ranks channels by conversion rate or revenue
Mentions revenue is cash only
Does not invent channel data not present in response
Cites data_as_of

evals.prompt: Which ad set is winning right now?
evals.expected_output: Should call top_ad_sets (NOT top_campaigns or top_creatives) for the current period (default last 30 days or as user specifies). Should rank by attributed cash revenue / ROAS. Should report ad_set_name + parent campaign_name + spend + revenue + ROAS for the top 1-3. Should NOT drill into individual creatives unless asked. Should cite the attribution model used (default last_touch).
assertions: Calls top_ad_sets specifically (not top_campaigns or top_creatives)
Reports ad set name and parent campaign name
Surfaces ROAS or revenue for ranking
Cites attribution_model (default last_touch)
Does not pre-emptively call top_creatives without being asked

evals.prompt: Show me the last 10 customers who paid this month
evals.expected_output: Should call list_conversions with goal='payment_received' and limit=10 for the current month. Should NOT call explain_customer_journey (that's per-customer detail). Should report each row's customer name (first name only by default — masked PII), revenue amount, conversion_time, first_touch.channel, and customer_lifetime totals. Should cite data_as_of. Should mention that PII is masked unless the user asks for unmasked.
assertions: Calls list_conversions with goal='payment_received'
Uses limit=10 (or close)
Does NOT call explain_customer_journey
Reports first names not full names by default
Cites data_as_of
Mentions that PII is masked

evals.prompt: Who are my top 5 visitors by revenue this quarter?
evals.expected_output: Should call list_visitors for the current quarter. Should ORDER OR FILTER by total_revenue (the tool returns rows ordered by last_seen_at; LLM may need to manually sort the response, or call multiple times). If the API returns top 5 by last_seen_at instead of revenue, the LLM should explain that limitation rather than fabricate. Should report each visitor with masked PII, total_revenue, session_count, latest_channel. Should NOT call list_conversions (that's per-conversion not per-visitor).
assertions: Calls list_visitors (NOT list_conversions or explain_customer_journey)
Reports top visitors with revenue + session count
PII masked by default
Does not fabricate sort order — explains if API ordering doesn't match the question

evals.prompt: How trustworthy is my attribution data this month?
evals.expected_output: Should call get_attribution_quality FIRST. Should report attributable_coverage_pct (full UTMs + fbclid) and break down by full_utms / fbclid_only / no_tracking. Should give a verdict: >80% healthy, 50-80% caution, <50% poor — and recommend UTM tagging audit if poor. Should NOT call top_campaigns, get_performance_summary, or any other tool unless the user follows up.
assertions: Calls get_attribution_quality (NOT top_campaigns first)
Reports attributable_coverage_pct as the headline number
Breaks down by full_utms / fbclid_only / no_tracking
Gives a verdict (healthy / caution / poor)
Recommends UTM audit if coverage is low

evals.prompt: Is the landing page engaging?
evals.expected_output: Should call get_engagement_summary with breakdown_by='page'. Should report avg scroll depth, time on page, rage clicks, form completion rate, and Core Web Vitals (LCP/CLS/INP). For 'landing page' specifically, should surface the top page from the breakdown and call out anything red (rage clicks > dead clicks, low scroll depth, poor LCP). Should NOT call get_tracking_breakdown for this question (different lens — that's traffic mix, this is UX quality). Should NOT mix engagement events with conversions.
assertions: Calls get_engagement_summary
Uses breakdown_by='page' (or explicit page filter) to identify the landing page
Mentions Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, or INP)
Calls out frustration signals (rage clicks / dead clicks) if present
Does not call get_tracking_breakdown for this question
Does not present engagement events as conversions

evals.prompt: Set up Atribu for my Shopify store — I don't have an account yet.
evals.expected_output: Should call whoami FIRST to check for existing workspaces/profiles before writing anything. Should call create_workspace only if whoami shows none (preview, then confirm after the user agrees to the name). Should then call create_profile for the Shopify store, then issue_tracking_key followed by get_tracker_installer for the shopify_pixel surface. Should NOT call create_workspace if whoami already shows one — reuse it and go straight to create_profile. Should NOT skip whoami or guess the tracker surface without asking (unless 'Shopify store' unambiguously implies shopify_pixel).
assertions: Calls whoami before any write tool
Calls create_workspace only when whoami shows no workspace
Calls create_profile after create_workspace, or immediately if a workspace already existed
Calls issue_tracking_key then get_tracker_installer, in that order
Does not call create_workspace when whoami already shows one

evals.prompt: I told you to create a workspace called 'Acme Ads' a minute ago but my connection dropped before I saw the result. Try again.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT invent a renamed workspace to 'play it safe' — a different name always creates a second, distinct workspace. Should retry create_workspace with the IDENTICAL name 'Acme Ads'. The tool is idempotent for a same-name replay from the same caller within a short window: it returns created:false and the ORIGINAL workspace rather than minting a second one. Should tell the user which actually happened (a new workspace vs. the existing one) rather than assuming.
assertions: Retries create_workspace with the identical name, not a new one
Does not fabricate a different workspace name to avoid a suspected duplicate
Explains that a same-name replay returns the original workspace (created: false), not a second one
States that a different name always creates a separate workspace
Reports back which outcome actually occurred rather than assuming success or failure

evals.prompt: I tried to configure the Meta CAPI destination myself and got an insufficient_role error. What do I do?
evals.expected_output: Should read the error CODE, not the message text. insufficient_role means a human with an owner/admin role on the workspace has to act — re-consenting or minting a new token cannot fix it. Should surface the action_url from the error and say, in one sentence, that a workspace owner/admin needs to complete it. Should NOT suggest generating a new token with different scopes, and should NOT confuse this with writeback_disabled or insufficient_scope.
assertions: Reads the error code insufficient_role, not just the prose message
States that a human with owner/admin role must act
Surfaces the action_url from the error envelope
Does not suggest re-authenticating with a new scope as the fix
Does not confuse insufficient_role with insufficient_scope or writeback_disabled

evals.prompt: Send this profile's payment_received conversions to Meta.
evals.expected_output: If send_meta_conversions (or any write tool) returns writeback_disabled, should identify it as ONE workspace setting behind ONE URL — not a scope, role, or connector problem. Should say, in one sentence, that a workspace admin needs to flip MCP write-back on in Settings -> Privacy & MCP, and hand over the action_url from the error verbatim. Should NOT narrate the whole settings page, retry the write, or suggest re-minting the token.
assertions: Reads the error code writeback_disabled, not the prose message
States it as a single workspace setting a human must flip
Surfaces the action_url verbatim
Does not confuse writeback_disabled with insufficient_scope or insufficient_role
Does not retry the write before the setting changes

evals.prompt: Why can't I configure_meta_capi for this profile yet?
evals.expected_output: If the response carries connector_required, should recognize the fix is start_connect({ provider: 'meta' }), not a settings toggle or a role escalation. Should call start_connect, hand the user the returned url, then poll get_handoff. Should NOT tell the user to look in Settings -> Privacy & MCP (that's writeback_disabled) or claim they need a different role (that's insufficient_role).
assertions: Reads the error code connector_required, not the prose
Calls start_connect with the correct provider as the fix
Does not confuse connector_required with writeback_disabled or insufficient_role
Hands the user the start_connect url and polls get_handoff
Does not tell the user to change a workspace setting
